judgments.reasoning_cat1: The identification uses an open-ended catch-all — "related topics such as oil drilling, technology and infrastructure" — appended to an enumerated list, and the exclusion "not including information concerning asset management and investment advice relating to stocks and bonds" has an uncertain reach across the listed items; the electronic-publications paragraph also omits the class designation (Class 9) that the other two paragraphs carry. These features make the boundary of the permitted goods and services genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 2 makes the covenant not to oppose turn precisely on "the goods and services as set forth in that application as amended pursuant to paragraph 1," so any imprecision here propagates into the operative covenant, and the recital frames the deal as resolving a potential opposition. That linkage creates a real, if not flat, tension when Petroleum Argus's actual use is compared with the amended recitation.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 1 — Amendment of PETROLEUM ARGUS Identification of Goods and Services

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant is expressly limited to the mark "as shown in that application ... as amended," but then adds the unbounded catch-all "or do any act or thing in derogation thereof," leaving open whether challenges to uses outside the amended recitation (e.g., ARGUS alone) are barred. That general-versus-specific tension is precisely the sort of scope question parties litigate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with paragraph 1's amended identification and paragraph 3's parallel ENERGY ARGUS covenant, the question arises whether the promise covers only conduct within the recited goods or all uses of the mark, which the entire-agreement clause in paragraph 6 does not resolve. There is a plausible whole-instrument reconciliation problem, though no flat contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 2 — Covenant Not to Oppose PETROLEUM ARGUS Application

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like paragraph 2, the specific limitation to the marks "as shown in the registrations for the goods and services as set forth in the registrations" is followed by the open phrase "do any act or thing in derogation thereof," whose reach is undefined. The registrations are identified by number, which makes the core definite, but the catch-all leaves an argument about conduct outside the registered scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in parallel with paragraph 2 and does not contradict it; the only friction is that paragraph 2's subject matter was narrowed by paragraph 1 while this one was not, which could be argued as an intended asymmetry. That is a modest coherence question rather than a conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 3 — Covenant Not to Oppose ENERGY ARGUS & Design Registrations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "This is the entire agreement and may be modified only in writing signed by both parties" is short but its two operative components are definite; the only softness is the absence of any statement about prior negotiations or the Background recitals. Nothing in the wording carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the "Background to Agreement" recitals and paragraphs 1–3: the merger clause tends to exclude extrinsic understandings about the scope of the ARGUS marks, which is a recurring source of argument in a trademark coexistence settlement of this brevity. Still, no operative provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence contains a plain drafting gap — "the performance of shall be governed" omits its object — and the trailing sentence "This provision extends to the United States, its territories and possessions" is opaque in a contract with a UK party. Both are mechanical/vagueness defects, though neither obviously changes the choice of New York law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the agreement addresses forum, law, or territorial scope, so there is no provision it can contradict. It is consistent with the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line successors-and-assigns clause using standard terms; "licensees" is unusual in the list but its meaning is plain. Nothing here invites competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no assignment restriction or other provision elsewhere in the agreement that this could conflict with. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Both parties will pay all their own costs in attorneys' fees" contains an evident mechanical slip — "in" for "and" — creating a question whether costs generally or only attorneys' fees are covered. The error is small but it does alter the scope of the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses fees or cost-shifting, so there is nothing for it to contradict. It fits the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The parties will agree to keep" is an agreement-to-agree formulation rather than a direct covenant, and the exception "as required by Court order and/or state and federal rules of civil procedure" is loosely bounded. These give some room for argument about whether and how far confidentiality binds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraphs 2 and 3 contemplate that the covenants may be asserted in Trademark Office or court proceedings, which necessarily involves disclosing the terms, but the express court-order and procedural-rules carve-out largely reconciles that. No direct conflict located.
